source_documents.title: Advantages of Mobile Liquid-Crystal Phase of AIE Luminogens for Effective Solid-State Emission

reference_evidence_units.quote: bulk 3 is crystalline at room temperature, which can be confirmed by multiple fine peaks in XRD data
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 3 (diethylene-oxide-chain TPE derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fast-dried crystalline bulk versus amorphous THF/water aggregates; room-temperature and heated PL, TCSPC, XRD and DSC.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Compound 3 is crystalline at room temperature, unlike LC compounds 1 and 2.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Figure 2 visually inspected; the source later interprets it as heterogeneous/polycrystalline, not one uniform single crystal.

reference_evidence_units.quote: 0.074 (bulk) vs. 0.22 (amorphous aggregate in THF/water solvent mixtures).
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 3 (diethylene-oxide-chain TPE derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fast-dried crystalline bulk versus amorphous THF/water aggregates; room-temperature and heated PL, TCSPC, XRD and DSC.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Bulk 3 emits less efficiently than its aqueous-solvent aggregate counterpart: yield 0.074 versus 0.22.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not transfer the enhancement trend or 0.33 yield of compound 2 to this target.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the blue-shifted emission of bulk 3 seems to reveal more tightly bound luminogens in aggre- gates
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 3 (diethylene-oxide-chain TPE derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fast-dried crystalline bulk versus amorphous THF/water aggregates; room-temperature and heated PL, TCSPC, XRD and DSC.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source associates bulk 3's blue shift with restricted structural relaxation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Indirect interpretation; stronger restriction does not predict higher yield here.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the decreasing AIE efficiency of bulk 3 is caused by the accelerated nonradiative rate
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 3 (diethylene-oxide-chain TPE derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fast-dried crystalline bulk versus amorphous THF/water aggregates; room-temperature and heated PL, TCSPC, XRD and DSC.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Yield/lifetime analysis attributes weaker bulk 3 emission to faster nonradiative decay. Table 1 gives knr 12 versus 2.8 x10^8 s^-1 in bulk versus solvent aggregates.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Phenomenological derived rates, not an independent direct measure of traps; room-temperature bulk lifetime is 0.75 ns.

reference_evidence_units.quote: there are various undesirable non-emissive elec- tronic states as compared to the monocrystalline condition
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 3 (diethylene-oxide-chain TPE derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fast-dried crystalline bulk versus amorphous THF/water aggregates; room-temperature and heated PL, TCSPC, XRD and DSC.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors propose surface traps and internal defects caused by rapid crystallization as extra loss channels in bulk 3.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: An inferred polycrystalline explanation, not directly resolved defect energies or populations.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The overall amplitude of fast decay components less than 1 ns in bulk 3 is 86.9%
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 3 (diethylene-oxide-chain TPE derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fast-dried crystalline bulk versus amorphous THF/water aggregates; room-temperature and heated PL, TCSPC, XRD and DSC.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The dominant sub-nanosecond decay fraction supports heterogeneous, rapidly deactivating bulk sites.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Text reports 86.9%; rounded Table 1 amplitudes 45.9% and 40.9% sum to 86.8%, so avoid implying more precision.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The discordance of increasing emission lifetime and more rapidly quenched emission intensity at 450 nm demonstrates reduced numbers of 450-nm-emissive luminogens
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 3 (diethylene-oxide-chain TPE derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fast-dried crystalline bulk versus amorphous THF/water aggregates; room-temperature and heated PL, TCSPC, XRD and DSC.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Above 140 C, the source interprets lifetime/intensity disagreement as redistribution from blue-emitting to red-emitting local environments.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Population/environment interpretation, not necessarily creation of an excimer; no J-assignment is established for 3.

reference_evidence_units.quote: which can be interpreted as a thermal perturbation followed by enlarged in- tramolecular motions
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 3 (diethylene-oxide-chain TPE derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fast-dried crystalline bulk versus amorphous THF/water aggregates; room-temperature and heated PL, TCSPC, XRD and DSC.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The decrease of red-edge lifetimes between 30 and 140 C is attributed to thermally activated internal motion.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The later reversal near isotropization reflects rearrangement, so the full temperature dependence is not monotonic RIM.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The source explicitly invokes restricted relaxation and thermal activation of motions, but these are insufficient to explain the poorer bulk yield.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Fast crystallization and heterogeneous/polycrystalline local environments are the central proposed source of quenching and thermal redistribution.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Increased knr and changing emissive-site populations explain lower bulk efficiency; these overlap with the defect/packing interpretation.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: The source explicitly invokes restricted relaxation and thermal activation of motions, but these are insufficient to explain the poorer bulk yield.

mechanism_decisions.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Fast crystallization and heterogeneous/polycrystalline local environments are the central proposed source of quenching and thermal redistribution.

mechanism_decisions.label: HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No guest binding, pore uptake or host inclusion mechanism is established; a solvent or self-assembly is not automatically host-guest chemistry.

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific CT or TICT mechanism is established in this extraction.

mechanism_decisions.label: ESIPT_PT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific excited-state proton-transfer pathway is established.

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No photoinduced electron-transfer quenching or turn-on is established; energy transfer and CT character are not by themselves PET.

mechanism_decisions.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: J-type coupling is assigned to 1 and 2, not 3. Defect-state loss and a red-edge redistribution are not independently an excimer/exciton assignment.

mechanism_decisions.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Increased knr and changing emissive-site populations explain lower bulk efficiency; these overlap with the defect/packing interpretation.

mechanism_decisions.label: TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No operative target-specific triplet or metal-mediated pathway is established.

mechanism_decisions.label: RACI_CI_ACCESS
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific conical-intersection mechanism is established; rotation restriction alone does not prove CI access.

mechanism_decisions.label: SOKR_ANTI_KASHA
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No higher-singlet-state emission or anti-Kasha mechanism is established; higher-state absorption alone is insufficient.
